newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says only the stable in first EMU wave.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says only the stable in first EMU wave.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said in the latest issue of BayernKurier, the newspaper of his Christian Social Union (CSU) party, that only equally stable countries could join the first wave of monetary union.

"A chain is only as strong as its weakest link," he said. "So, at the beginning of the monetary union, only countries that are equally stable can join. Convergence determines the schedule, in every single country."
He added that the application of the Maastricht Treaty rules in determining economic convergence among European Union members was indispensible.

Chancellor Helmut Kohl, under pressure to take a hard line on EMU from Bavarian premier and Eurosceptic Edmund Stoiber, made clear on Tuesday that Germany wanted a strict interpretation of the fiscal targets for monetary union.
The Maastricht Treaty targets for countries hoping to qualify for the start of monetary union in 1999 include a three percent limit for budget deficits as a ratio of gross domestic product in 1997.

With countries like Germany and France in danger of overshooting the deficit criterion, Stoiber has been calling for a delay of monetary union, fearing the euro currency would not be as strong as the mark unless the treaty's entry goals are met.
